mismatches: The mass is 22.19 g, which exceeds the requirement R7 (mass <= 20 g).
The design document specifies a tapered I-beam style arm to maximize second moment of area, but the rendered part is a simple rectangular prism/block with no tapering or I-beam profile.
systemic: The requirement R6 (stiffness) asks for an I <= 1.0 mm^4, which contradicts the strength requirements and standard engineering logic for a drone arm; however, even if interpreted as I >= 1.0, the design document's claim of being an 'I-beam style' is not reflected in the actual geometry produced.
gate.summary: The part fails the mass requirement and does not implement the intended tapered I-beam geometry described in the design document.

mismatches: R1 violation: The part consists of 3 separate solids instead of one single valid solid (n_solids=3).
R2 violation: The bounding box starts at x = -2.5, failing the 'minimum x = 0' requirement.
R3 violation: The frame attachment holes are misplaced; they appear to be centered around y=5 instead of y=+/-6 (as seen in cylindrical_faces data).
R4 violation: The motor mount holes are incorrectly placed at x=132 instead of the specified x=120.
Design Concept mismatch: The part is a solid rectangular beam rather than the intended hollowed I-beam structure described in the design document.
systemic: The design concept of an extremely thin web (0.1 mm) to meet stiffness requirements is likely unprintable and structurally unsound for a drone arm.
gate.summary: The part fails almost all geometric and structural requirements, including being multiple solids, having incorrect hole placements, and failing to implement the intended I-beam geometry.

mismatches: R3: The frame attachment holes at (6, +-6) are missing; only one hole is visible in the cylindrical faces data and render.
R4: The motor mount features (four 3.2mm holes and one 6mm shaft clearance hole) are completely missing from the rendered part.

R2/Design Document: The design document specifies a height of ~0.7mm at x=20 to satisfy R6, but the bounding box shows a total height of 8.0 mm, indicating the part is much thicker than intended for the stiffness constraint.
systemic: The design document acknowledges a mathematical impossibility: satisfying both R5 (strength) and R6 (stiffness) within the allowed width envelope (|y| <= 16). The priority given to R6 results in a part that will fail catastrophically under load.
gate.summary: The rendered part is missing all required mounting and clearance holes and fails to implement the specific geometry intended to meet the contradictory stiffness/strength constraints.

mismatches: R7 (Mass) violation: The measured mass is 21.91 g, which exceeds the maximum requirement of 20 g.
gate.summary: The part follows the design concept but fails the mass constraint specified in R7.

mismatches: The motor mount section (x=110 to 130) is not a widened flange as described; it appears to be the same thin profile as the rest of the arm.
The motor shaft clearance hole at (120, 0) and the four motor bolt holes are missing from the render.
The frame attachment holes at (6, +-6) are not visible in the render.
systemic: The design attempts to satisfy a stiffness constraint (I <= 1.0) and a strength constraint (sigma <= 30 MPa) that are mathematically contradictory for this geometry; the resulting part is too thin to support the motor load.
gate.summary: The rendered part fails to include all required mounting holes and does not implement the widened motor mount flange described in the design document, while the underlying design concept is physically non-viable due to contradictory constraints.
